response.headline: No strong cause was found; the service measures well here [insufficient_data].

causes.explanation: Measured speeds are strong at the point and nearby [speed_cell][speed_1km][speed_neighbours], multiple operators have sites within 5 km [operators_5km], and clear lines of sight exist to EE, O2 and Vodafone sites about 0.1 km away [los_ee][los_o2][los_vodafone][network_comparison]. No severe weather warning is active [met_office_warnings], so no persistent or current cause can be supported.

actions.text: Try the best network: Vodafone is likely best here [network_comparison].
Use Wi-Fi calling indoors if available.
Check the address on Ofcom's mobile coverage checker: https://www.ofcom.org.uk/mobile-coverage-checker
Emergency calls work on any available network.

response.best_network: Vodafone is likely best here, with a clear line of sight to a site 0.1 km east confirmed by Ofcom's licence register. EE and O2 also have clear lines to sites 0.1 km away; EE and O2 operators are inferred from crowd-sourced data rather than confirmed by Ofcom's licence register [network_comparison][los_ee][los_o2][los_vodafone]. Three has a site 190 m south with a small terrain margin, so its signal is likely weakened, not necessarily lost [los_three].
limitations: Sites are approximate; antenna heights assumed where not confirmed; Ofcom figures are area-level.
Causes are inferred from public data, not confirmed: operators' network data is not public.
Ookla speeds are quarterly aggregates with no time-of-day detail; congestion can only be inferred.
No address-level Ofcom coverage; Ofcom figures are for the whole constituency and are predictions.
Mast sites are approximate (crowd-sourced OpenCelliD, OpenStreetMap, Ofcom's licence register) and incomplete, so 'no sites found' is weak evidence.
Line of sight uses a surface model (trees and buildings included) and mostly assumed antenna heights; blocked means a weaker signal, not no signal.
